raw_case_text:
A 42-year-old male presented to the medical emergency department with complaints of weakness and significant weight loss over 1 year. He had episodes of low-grade fever in the past year, for which the patient was treated for pulmonary tuberculosis 2 years back. At present, he was again put on antitubercular therapy (ATT) for the past 1 month; however, no improvement was noted and hence the patient was referred to our hospital. There was no significant family history. On general physical examination, the patient was found to be thin built, pale, and afebrile with abdominal distension. Left submandibular and left axillary lymph nodes were enlarged and measured 1.5 cm in diameter. Mild hepatosplenomegaly was noted, however no fluid thrill could be discerned. Ultrasound abdomen revealed enlarged multiple conglomerate of mesenteric lymph nodes with the largest node measuring 22 mm x 18 mm. Clinical chemistry revealed A:G reversal with total protein of 9.5 g%, albumin of 2.0 g%, globulin of 7.5 g%, and A:G ratio of 1:3.75. Other parameters of liver function test and kidney function test were found to be within normal limits. Complete hemogram revealed pancytopenia with hemoglobin: 6 g%, total leukocyte count: 1800/muL, differential leukocyte count: polymorphs 47%, lymphocytes 51%, eosinophils 1%, monocytes 1%, platelets: 48,000/muL, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 50 mm/h. Peripheral smear revealed the presence of rouleaux; however, no hemoparasite was noted.
Fine needle aspiration cytology was performed on the left submandibular and axillary lymph nodes, which yielded thick aspirate. Smears prepared showed few epithelioid cell granulomas interspersed with discrete and aggregates of histiocytes in a background of reactive lymphoid cells and many plasma cells. Numerous intracellular as well as extracellular amastigote forms of Leishmania species were seen [Figure 1]. In view of strong clinical suspicion, Ziehl-Neelsen staining for acid-fast bacilli (AFB) was also done which came out to be negative. Both polymerase chain reaction for Mycobacterium tuberculosis and AFB culture yielded negative result. Later on, rK39 antigen was also found to be positive. Bone marrow examination (both aspirate and biopsy) revealed a prominence of plasma cells and histiocytes along with infiltration by numerous intracellular as well as extracellular amastigote forms of Leishmania spp. Average parasite density (APD) of 5+, i.e., 10-100 Leishman-Donovan (LD) bodies/field, was noted in the bone marrow aspirate (BMA) [Figure 2]. In view of high APD, the patient's human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) status was evaluated which showed positive serology. Immune status evaluation revealed a low CD4 count; 28/muL (reference range: 400-1600/muL). The patient was started on intravenous amphotericin B along with highly active antiretroviral therapy. Improvement was noted after 14 days of treatment (CD4 count: 36/muL). Subsequent bone marrow evaluations revealed a significant fall in APD and clinical improvement in patient's health; weight gain, improved appetite, and rise in CD4 counts.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 42-year-old male presented with progressive weakness, significant weight loss, and low-grade fever for 1 year.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 42-year-old male presented to the emergency department with a 1-year history of weakness, significant unintentional weight loss, and recurrent episodes of low-grade fever. He had been treated for pulmonary tuberculosis 2 years previously. For the preceding month, he had been restarted on empirical antitubercular therapy (ATT) without improvement, prompting referral to a tertiary care hospital.
subjective.past_medical_history: Treated for pulmonary tuberculosis 2 years prior; recent 1-month course of empirical antitubercular therapy. Family history non-contributory. Prior other medications and allergies not documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Generalized weakness, marked weight loss, low-grade fever, abdominal distension. Denied cough, hemoptysis, diarrhea, or rash.

objective.physical_examination: Thin-built, pale, afebrile male with abdominal distension. Left submandibular and left axillary lymph nodes were palpable, measuring 1.5 cm in diameter each. Abdominal examination revealed mild hepatosplenomegaly without fluid thrill.
objective.routine_investigations: Pancytopenia on complete hemogram: hemoglobin 6.0 g/dL, total leukocyte count 1,800/muL (polymorphs 47%, lymphocytes 51%, eosinophils 1%, monocytes 1%), platelets 48,000/muL, ESR 50 mm/h. Peripheral smear showed rouleaux formation without hemoparasites. Serum protein electrophoresis revealed marked A:G reversal: total protein 9.5 g/dL, albumin 2.0 g/dL, globulin 7.5 g/dL (A:G ratio 1:3.75). Liver and kidney function tests otherwise normal. HIV serology was positive; CD4+ T-cell count was 28/muL (reference range 400-1,600/muL).
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal ultrasonography showed multiple enlarged conglomerate mesenteric lymph nodes (largest 22 x 18 mm) and hepatosplenomegaly. Fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) of left submandibular and axillary lymph nodes revealed epithelioid granulomas, discrete histiocytic aggregates, plasma cells, and numerous intracellular and extracellular microorganisms; Ziehl-Neelsen stain for acid-fast bacilli was negative; PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis and AFB cultures were negative. Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy showed prominent plasma cells and histiocytes with abundant intracellular and extracellular microorganisms.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive Diagnosis: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) with generalized lymphadenopathy in a patient with newly diagnosed advanced HIV-1 coinfection (AIDS).
Diagnostic Confirmation: FNAC of lymph nodes and bone marrow aspirate/biopsy demonstrated abundant intracellular and extracellular Leishmania amastigotes (average parasite density 5+, 10-100 LD bodies/field in BMA); rK39 rapid antigen test was positive; HIV serology positive with CD4+ count of 28/muL.
Differentials Ruled Out: Recurrent/disseminated tuberculosis and tuberculous lymphadenitis (negative ZN stains, negative MTB PCR, negative AFB culture, clinical failure on ATT), lymphoma, and visceral histoplasmosis.
Treatment & Clinical Course: Empirical ATT was discontinued. Initiated on intravenous amphotericin B combined with HAART. After 14 days of therapy, CD4+ count improved to 36/muL. Follow-up bone marrow aspirates demonstrated significant clearance of parasite density, accompanied by appetite recovery, weight gain, hematologic reconstitution, and progressive immune recovery.
